Lung adenocarcinoma: reproducible expression differences and survival follow-up

Completed analysis · October 5, 2026 · Prepared for Hamza Ahmed

50matched TCGA pairs
19,026expression-filtered genes
10 / 10external expression directions agree
0 / 10corrected-significant survival candidates

What this project found

A public-data reanalysis of TCGA-LUAD compared tumor and non-tumor tissue in 50 matched patients. Of 19,026 expression-filtered genes, 13,821 passed FDR <0.05 and convergence checks; 4,528 also had an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1. Ten expression-selected genes showed the same direction and passed ten-test FDR <0.05 in the independent GSE31210 microarray cohort. Age- and stage-adjusted overall-survival analyses included 465 TCGA patients (169 deaths) and 204 GEO patients (30 deaths). No candidate passed survival FDR <0.05 in either cohort. These findings support reproducible tissue-expression differences, but do not establish prognostic biomarkers.

Interpretation: A gene can differ strongly between tumor and non-tumor tissue without reliably predicting which patients live longer. This study demonstrates that distinction. A nonsignificant survival result is not proof that an association is absent.

Cohort and quality checks

The GDC inventory contained 601 files across 518 patients: 540 primary-tumor, 59 non-tumor, and 2 recurrent-tumor files. File counts were not treated as independent patients. The audit excluded all 35 files in ambiguous patient-condition groups, 12 further files with specified quality/treatment annotations, and the 2 recurrent tumors. Of 552 eligible files, 6 normal files lacked an eligible tumor pair. The final download comprised 496 unique primary tumors plus 50 paired normal samples.

All 546 files passed their published MD5 checks. Gene IDs and annotation aligned exactly across samples; counts were nonnegative integers. All files stated GENCODE v36 and shared one GDC workflow version. Total gene-assigned reads ranged from 18.0 to 103.7 million per sample. No samples were removed after inspecting gene significance.

The differential-expression design had 100 samples and 51 independent columns: patient effects plus tissue condition. Raw unstranded counts were used for inference. All paired samples had the same source-center code, but 11 pairs had different plate codes. A separate same-plate sensitivity analysis retained 39 pairs. Raw-read mapping quality and detailed sequencing batches were not independently reanalyzed.

Paired differential expression

PyDESeq2 0.5.4 fitted the model ~ patient + condition, with tumor versus normal as the explicit contrast. Genes required at least 10 counts in at least 50 samples. Benjamini-Hochberg correction controlled the tested-gene false discovery rate. Sixty-one genes failed at least one convergence check and were excluded from supported significance and follow-up selection; original estimates and flags remain available.

Among successfully fitted genes, 6,722 were higher and 7,099 lower in tumors at FDR <0.05. The more descriptive threshold of FDR <0.05 and |log2FC| ≥1 retained 4,528 genes. Fold changes are unshrunk estimates. These are observational bulk-tissue differences and can reflect differences in cell composition or tumor purity.

Independent expression follow-up

The frozen candidate rule selected unique-symbol protein-coding genes with normalized mean ≥100, FDR <0.05 and |log2FC| ≥1, ranked by absolute Wald statistic. The resulting list was PYCR1, SLC6A4, RTKN2, FABP4, SERTM1, FHL1, AGER, RGCC, KANK3, and RAMP2.

GSE31210 included 226 primary lung adenocarcinomas and 20 normal tissues. Its MAS5-normalized array intensities were log2-transformed, uniquely annotated probes were mapped to genes, and multiple unambiguous probes were averaged on the log scale. All ten candidates agreed in direction with TCGA and passed ten-test BH FDR <0.05 in exploratory Welch comparisons. PYCR1 was higher in tumors; the other nine were lower. Normal-to-tumor patient matching was not established in this cohort, so Welch independence is an assumption and external expression p-values should be interpreted cautiously.

For all ten candidates, paired Wilcoxon sensitivity tests supported the same direction at ten-test FDR <0.05 in both all 50 TCGA pairs and the 39 same-plate pairs. This supports robustness to that particular technical concern, without resolving all possible confounding.

Survival: no corrected-significant candidate

Curated TCGA-CDR outcomes matched all 496 selected primary-tumor patients. Thirty-one patients were excluded from complete-case analysis: 13 lacked a usable positive survival time, 19 lacked age, and 8 lacked stage, with overlapping reasons. The retained 465 patients had 169 deaths and stages I/II/III/IV distributed as 251/114/76/24.

The GEO cohort retained 204 patients after the submitter's 22 prognosis exclusions, with 30 deaths. Separate Cox models tested each candidate continuously, adjusted for age and categorical stage. TCGA used log2(TPM+1); GEO used log2 array intensity. Expression was standardized within each cohort. No survival-driven cutoff or multigene prediction score was optimized.

No gene reached FDR <0.05 in either cohort. AGER had nominal TCGA p=0.026 but q=0.240. FABP4 had nominal GEO p=0.0059 but q=0.0586. Neither is a corrected-significant replicated prognostic finding.

Expression proportional-hazards checks did not reject after ten-test correction. Several TCGA stage terms showed nominal proportional-hazards concerns; a stage-stratified sensitivity model again found no gene at FDR <0.05. Seven GEO candidates showed quadratic-shape diagnostic signals after correction: PYCR1, SLC6A4, SERTM1, FHL1, RGCC, KANK3, and RAMP2. With only 30 GEO deaths, these post-fit diagnostics highlight uncertainty in simple linear hazard assumptions; they are not validated nonlinear biomarker discoveries. Excluding annotation-positive TCGA cases retained 407 patients and 144 deaths, with no corrected-significant candidate.

Pathway context

Preranked enrichment used converged-gene Wald statistics, 50 Hallmark 2020 gene sets, 1,000 permutations, and seed 20261005. Duplicate symbols were resolved using highest normalized mean expression, independently of significance. 24 gene sets had enrichment FDR <0.05. Positive enrichment included E2F targets, G2-M checkpoint, MYC targets, glycolysis, and DNA repair. Negative enrichment included myogenesis and TNF-alpha signaling via NF-kB.

These patterns are consistent with differences in proliferative, metabolic, and tissue-composition programs; the analysis cannot distinguish cellular composition from within-cell regulation or establish causal pathway activation. Zero values in permutation-estimated FDR output mean none observed in the sampled null tail, not a true probability of zero. Gene-set permutation inference does not fully account for intergene correlation.

Limitations and supportable claims

  • This is an AI-assisted public-data reanalysis, not a prospective clinical study or a claim of novel biomarker discovery.
  • TCGA non-tumor tissue is not healthy-volunteer tissue. Tumor purity, immune/stromal composition, treatment, smoking, and residual technical effects can influence expression and prognosis.
  • Excluding ambiguous samples improves identity certainty but can introduce selection bias. Complete-case survival analysis can also be biased by missingness.
  • GEO was stage I-II, used a different assay, and had only 30 eligible deaths. TCGA outcomes use a historical 2018 freeze. Cohort endpoint origins and follow-up contexts are not identical.
  • Seven GEO genes had nonlinearity diagnostic signals; the linear-HR summaries are limited. No clinical risk score, predictive accuracy, or treatment decision rule was validated.
  • Independent tissue-expression concordance supports reproducibility of direction. It does not by itself support prognosis, causality, novelty, or clinical usefulness.

Supportable conclusion: A reproducible, patient-aware analysis found tumor-associated expression differences and external directional agreement for ten candidates, while corrected survival testing did not establish prognostic associations under the specified models.

Reproducibility and sources

The project contains source scripts, frozen dependencies, raw-count matrices for the paired cohort, complete gene results, sample exclusions, candidate expression values, clinical eligibility tables, model diagnostics, and reference checksums. Large downloaded inputs remain in the local work folder and can be retrieved again with the included scripts. The package contains no private credentials.
